note: Cross-asset provenance log for sprites that did NOT go through the normal per-request /sprite pipeline (docs/data/art/requests/<id>.json + RawArt/Renders/<id>/r<rev>/manifest.json). Assets generated through that pipeline record their own provenance there instead -- this file exists for the exceptions, so a reader doesn't have to guess why one texture in Content/Sprites has no matching request.
ramp_departure: T_Soldier_Knight and T_Soldier_Archer are, as of task-050 rev 4, a DELIBERATE, OWNER-DIRECTED departure from the locked 4-value Demichrome ramp (docs/art/aesthetic-direction.md, locked 2026-07-10) -- full PixelLab colour, no quantize pass, for the Unit Cam panel specifically. This is NOT drift and should NOT be 'corrected' back to the ramp by a future pass. Owner's words: 'use the full color models we have on pixel lab.' Scope of the departure, stated precisely so it isn't over-read: it applies ONLY to these two Unit Cam retinue textures. It does NOT apply to T_Swarm_2bit, T_Hero_Vanguard, T_Unit_Retinue, the six retired T_Soldier_01..06 militia variants, or anything the world renderer draws -- those still render through M_PP_Demichrome and are quantized by the post-process pass regardless of their own source pixels. The reason full colour is viable here at all: the Unit Cam panel is UMG and draws AFTER post-processing, so nothing downstream quantizes it -- which is exactly why every sprite in it had to be PRE-quantized before this change, and exactly why removing that pre-quantize now displays PixelLab's output as-authored. This file, not docs/art/**, is the record of the decision -- docs/art/** is the art director's and a canon ramp change is the owner's call, made verbally, not a file either of the last two task-050 rounds was authorized to edit.
history: task-050 rev 1 (2026-07-27): built six 48px soldier-roster variants (T_Soldier_01..06, docs/art/soldier-roster-v1.md) into the Unit Cam retinue, plus this archer proxy at 48px to match, quantized to the Demichrome ramp.
task-050 rev 2 (2026-07-27): fixed the archer's Dark-dominance via a shadow lift (still ramp-quantized, still 48px).

task-050 rev 3 (2026-07-27/28): owner rejected the 48px approach on sight -- 'we degraded with the units again. I only want my high resolution units for the retinue. So the archer model and the knight model we had.' The six variants were dropped from the panel (files kept, unreferenced by UnitCamProjector.cpp) and replaced with exactly two high-resolution units, still ramp-quantized: this archer repacked at native resolution with the same shadow lift, and a new knight.

task-050 rev 4 (2026-07-28): owner reviewed the rev-3 capture and diagnosed it as still reading mushy/soft-edged. Direction: 'use the full color models we have on pixel lab' -- drop quantization entirely for these two units. This revision removes the shadow lift, pixelpipe.quantize_array, and the pale-to-bone safety clamp from both; the sheets are now the raw PixelLab rotations with only a crop/centre/pack step, no recolouring at all. See ramp_departure above and each entry's conversion/qc sections below.

task-050 rev 5 (2026-07-28): owner, on the rev-4 capture: 'the units they are a little scaled oddly. Can they be more broad?' Root cause found in the PACKING, not the draw code: every rotation's real alpha content measures only ~23-46px per side (max 43x46 across both characters, all directions), inside an 88-92px source canvas that PixelLab renders with a large, roughly-symmetric transparent margin on all sides -- the rev 3/4 cell (96x96, sized to the source canvas) therefore left real content filling only ~45-48% of the cell, drawn at the same on-screen box size as the blank padding around it. Fixed by shrinking the cell to 56x60 (fits the measured max content with >=10px margin on every side) -- a crop, not a resize: no content pixel is scaled or resampled, only the amount of surrounding blank canvas kept in the packed sheet changes. Also added a new live CVar, Emberkeep.UnitCamProj.SoldierAspect (width-only multiplier, default 1, in Saved/SwarmExecOnPlay.txt), for further taste-tuning on top of the fix -- left at 1 because the packing fix alone already reads broad and crisp in a capture; the dial exists for the owner to keep adjusting without a rebuild, not because 1 was a guess.

entries.in_panel_lighting_finding: Reported honestly per the owner's ask, not fixed unilaterally: the Unit Cam panel applies its own per-body grey-multiply lighting (flame-distance falloff, a facing-based front/back term, a retinue floor of 0.28x) UNDERNEATH whatever texture is bound -- this was designed against the old 4-value quantized sprites, where even the dimmest tint still lands on a legible palette step. Against full-colour source art, the SAME multiply compounds with the source's own dark values (hood, leather, armor recesses) and can crush a body toward near-black at typical panel framing distances, well short of full PixelLab saturation. A unit close to the bearer and facing the flame reads clearly; one further out or facing away reads dim and detail-poor. This is a property of the existing lighting model meeting full-colour art for the first time, not of this texture -- flagged for a deliberate decision (e.g. a higher floor or a lighter multiply for these two sprite sets specifically), not changed here since it wasn't asked for and touches shading shared with brood. UPDATE, rev 5: the cell-size fix (see history) made units read noticeably better in the SAME lighting -- more of each drawn box is now real content rather than padding, so a dim tint has more actual pixels to be visible on. This softened the practical impact of the finding but did not address its cause; the finding itself still stands and the same follow-up is still open.

entries.swap_path: Replacing this is a texture import + this manifest entry, NOT a code change. entries.what_was_not_assembled: attack, attack_v2 and hit are downloaded and archived but NOT wired into the sheet or the C++ selection logic. They are south-only, and the panel's camera orbits freely -- integrating them would mean either (a) snapping a unit to a south-facing attack pose regardless of which way the camera is actually looking at it (a visible, wrong-looking direction pop), or (b) building a combat-state-aware selection path (reading SwarmAnim::AttackBit/HitFlashBit) scoped to south only, real added complexity with an inconsistent payoff (7/8 directions still would not attack-animate). Left unintegrated rather than half-built, same call as rev 3 -- unaffected by the full-colour change. Flagged as a real, cheap-to-reach follow-up: the frames already exist, spent, and archived.
